craft_notes: Sthāyin: the rhetorical four (mutes, meditates, worships, pleased — the questions that unask ritual). Rows: row 1 (four uncut — never trim a ladder). Rupture: dash after told — state, then unasking. Close: lord? (the pleased-question closes on the vocative: whom would it please). Rejected: answering any of the four — killed: rhetorical kept (per argmap, the verse unasks); 'who is worthy' — killed: who mutes kept (the muting-word is the verse's own first gate).

lines: In this state told — who mutes, who meditates, who worships?
who is pleased, O great lord?
l4.sanskrit_cite: evamuktavyavasthāyāṃ japyate ko japaś ca kaḥ | dhyāyate ko mahānātha pūjyate kaś ca tṛpyati

reads_against.argmap: Who mutes, meditates, worships? → The rhetorical four: in this state, who at all mutes and worships?
c1_essence: Who mutes, meditates, worships, pleased? Rhetorical.
reads_against.c1_rasa: vīra with śānta (resolve closing the practice arc)
